subject: PrivDep DPA: Custody model, operator access limits, and geo-egress controls
messages:
From: Erik Solheim <erik@medisoft.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-11-02T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Private deployment DPA questions (VPC / BYOK)

Vanessa —

Thanks for the call last week. We reviewed the draft DPA you sent and have a few open items that are blocking our security/compliance sign-off for a private VPC deployment with customer-managed keys (BYOK). I attached the DPA we received (dpa-draft-medisoft-v1.pdf) and a short subprocessors matrix showing expected vendor categories. High-level items: 

1) Key custody & operator access: we need explicit language that Redwood will not hold customer master keys and that any operator access to decrypted data requires an audit ticket and our explicit consent (apart from emergency break-glass).
2) Break-glass & forensics: what is the process, and can we require that all forensics operate on copies inside our VPC with operator actions recorded?
3) Subprocessors: please confirm the list of subprocessors that would touch telemetry/ops for private deployments (we expect a narrower set than hosted).
4) Cross-border transfers: Medisoft cannot allow backups or log exports to leave the US without prior approval. Please advise how Redwood can guarantee that.

Can your team propose language we can redline? Also loop in procurement when you have the redline.

Attachments: [Attachment: dpa-draft-medisoft-v1.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)], [Attachment: subprocessors-list-medisoft.xlsx (XLSX, 58KB)]

Thanks,
Erik
Erik Solheim
Senior Counsel, Medisoft Health
legal@medisoft.com
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Erik Solheim <erik@medisoft.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-11-03T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment DPA questions (VPC / BYOK)

Erik —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answers here and we can provide a redline by end of day Thursday: 

- Keys: Redwood supports BYOK for Private (VPC/on-prem). Our standard private-deploy addendum specifies that customer retains root KMS keys; Redwood may hold ephemeral signing keys for orchestration but cannot decrypt model input/output unless explicitly authorised per the emergency procedure. We will draft a clause: "No access to customer master keys; operator access to decrypted content requires documented consent and ticketing."

- Break-glass: we agree to a documented break-glass process. We propose that operator forensic sessions run against a copy of data within the customer VPC or an isolated forensic image accessible only with a jointly-managed access token, with all operator commands logged. Marcus will add technical controls.

- Subprocessors: Redwood private deployments use fewer subprocessors; the attached matrix will be updated. We can include a commitment to notify Medisoft within 30 days of any new subprocessor and require your approval for any with potential data egress paths.

- Geo-egress: we can contractually restrict backups and logs to US regions and prohibit exporter agents leaving specified ASNs without approval. We will propose specific export controls language.

Next steps: I'll coordinate legal redline + a tech appendix from Marcus. Can we schedule a 45-minute call Friday to walk the redline and the operator control playbook?

Best,
Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
[Attachment: draft-action-items.md (TXT, 3KB)]
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Erik Solheim <erik@medisoft.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-11-04T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Technical appendix: operator access, telemetry, and audit controls

Erik / team —

Following up with more detail on the technical controls Vanessa summarized. Below are proposed operational commitments we can put into an appendix to the DPA for private deployments: 

- Key custody: Customer supplies and manages the KMS root keys (BYOK). Redwood components that require short-lived keys will use keys derived from customer KMS via an ephemeral grant; Redwood will not persist customer master keys.

- Operator access & break-glass: 
  - All operator sessions must be initiated via a documented ticket (ticket ID in any logs) except for lifecycle-critical automated failover.
  - For forensic investigations, we will operate on snapshots exported to a customer-controlled analysis workspace (within the customer's VPC or a mutually agreed on-prem enclave). Any access will be read-only unless you grant write privileges for remediation.
  - All operator commands, SSH sessions, and console activity will be logged to an append-only audit stream with HMAC-backed integrity; Redwood will provide logs on request for 90 days by default and 7 years for legal hold with a separate addendum.

- Telemetry & metrics: 
  - Usage telemetry that could contain identifiers will be stripped at the agent boundary; we can restrict certain telemetry (e.g., prompt text) from being forwarded off-network.
  - We will provide a per-route/tenant telemetry toggle to disable any telemetry that includes unredacted content.

- Subprocessor scope: for Private we expect infra providers (Kubernetes distribution vendor), on-call support partner, and a narrow set of backup/storage vendors. We will provide a list and a change-notice process (30 days) and allow Medisoft the right to escalate to a commercial review for any new subprocessor with data egress risk.

I attached a short runbook excerpt and sample audit log format for your review.

Attachments: [Attachment: privdep-operator-playbook-snippet.txt (TXT, 12KB)], [Attachment: sample-audit-log.json (TXT, 4KB)]

Happy to walk through the appendix on Friday.

– Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com
From: Erik Solheim <erik@medisoft.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@medisoft.com <procurement@medisoft.com>
Date: 2025-11-05T14:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Technical appendix: operator access, telemetry, and audit controls

Thanks Marcus — that level of detail is helpful. A few clarifications and asks before we take a redline to procurement: 

- Please add explicit contractual language that prevents Redwood support staff or subprocessors from initiating outbound log exports to non-US regions without Medisoft sign-off.
- For the HMAC-backed audit stream: we need the format and an example of the verification process so our DFIR team can validate integrity.
- Legal hold: Medisoft may require preservation for litigation. We need retention and export procedures for legal hold requests (how we get read-only copies, what format, turnaround SLA).
- Escrow/Key recovery: we need a proposed escrow model if customer keys are lost — who triggers, what authorization is required, and can we require multi-party approval (e.g., Medisoft + third-party escrow) for any recovery operation?

If you can draft those items into the DPA addendum, procurement will accept a commercial redline, and we can aim to execute next week.

Erik
Senior Counsel, Medisoft Health
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Erik Solheim <erik@medisoft.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-11-06T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: DPA addendum draft and next steps

Erik —

Thanks for the clear asks. Attached is an addendum draft that incorporates:
- Operator access clause with ticketing and explicit prohibition on outbound exports without customer sign-off.
- HMAC audit stream appendix with sample verification steps.
- Legal-hold preservation workflow and turnaround SLAs (initial copy within 48 hours; forensic export within 7 calendar days for standard requests, accelerated on negotiated SLA).
- Two escrow options: (1) multi-party escrow (Medisoft + independent escrow agent) for root key recovery; (2) customer-managed recovery via documented offline backup only.

Attachments: [Attachment: dpa-addendum-privdep-v2.pdf (PDF, 220KB)], [Attachment: subproc-consent-form.pdf (PDF, 18KB)]

Proposed next steps:
- Please review the addendum and confirm any redlines by Tuesday 11/11.
- If agreeable, procurement can accept the form and we will route for signatures (DocuSign link provided).
- I'll schedule a 45-minute technical walkthrough on Friday 11/07 (invite to follow).

If anything urgent, ping me or Vanessa.

Regards,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com
